html:
Vostok 1 was the first human spaceflight. On 12 April 1961 the Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin was launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan and made one orbit of the Earth.

The flight lasted under two hours. Gagarin's capsule was controlled automatically, in case a human could not work in weightlessness. On the way back he ejected from the capsule a few kilometres up and landed by parachute in a field in southern Russia, where he met a startled farm woman and her granddaughter.

It came four years after Sputnik 1 and was another triumph for the designer Sergei Korolev, whose name was kept secret. Gagarin became a world hero overnight. Three weeks later the American Alan Shepard made a short flight that did not reach orbit, and President Kennedy soon promised a Moon landing. The space race led to the first Moon landing in 1969.
sum: Vostok 1 was the first human spaceflight. On 12 April 1961 the Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin was launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan and made one orbit of the Earth.
